observations: Photos 0 and 1 show the same used inline four-cylinder petrol engine from the front, taken from almost the same angle: aluminium valve cover and timing cover, crank pulley, idler, water pump pulley, power steering pulley and alternator.
Photos 0 and 1: a barcode sticker on the timing cover is only partly legible (fragments like 'A62' and '047'); it does not give a readable maker or engine code.
Photos 0 and 1: a small label with the letter 'E' on the valve cover; no maker logo is visible on the engine.
Photo 2: top view of the valve cover with the oil filler cap and four open spark plug wells; the ignition coils are not fitted.
Photo 2: intake side with hoses and wiring still attached; a red paint mark and a handwritten number on the valve cover.
All photos: heavy dirt, oil staining and surface rust on the brackets and mounts; the engine sits on a wet workshop floor among other parts.
All photos carry a 'POSTED ON JIJI' and 'UCHENNA' watermark, so this is a dealer's advert photo.
No photo shows the block stamp, the underside, the sump, the dipstick or the engine running.

identity.kind: used 4-cylinder petrol car engine (seller says Toyota, for RAV4 and similar)
read_from: photos 0 to 2 show a 4-cylinder engine but no readable maker or engine code; the barcode sticker in photos 0 and 1 is not legible

claims.claim: Complete engine for Toyota vehicles such as RAV4 (second generation XA20)
claims.evidence: No Toyota logo or engine code can be read in any photo; fitment to a RAV4 cannot be checked without the block stamp.
Photo 2 shows the four spark plug wells with no ignition coils fitted.
Origin cannot be shown by photos of the engine.
No clip of the engine running is provided.
An engine out of a car carries no odometer; nothing in the photos shows mileage.
No close-up of the head and sump joints and bolts; heavy grime in photos 0 to 2 neither proves nor disproves it.

risks.risk: Engine code and displacement unknown; this sets which engine it is and what it is worth.
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the engine code stamped on the block, readable.
risks.if_unproven: not priceable; identity must be read first

risks.risk: Engine may not run, may knock, burn oil or have low compression.
risks.proof: Clip of the engine running on a test stand from cold start with sound, plus a compression reading on each cylinder.
risks.if_unproven: as a non-running core for parts

risks.risk: Ignition coils are missing and other parts on the unseen sides may be missing too.
risks.proof: Photos of all four sides and the underside, with the coils and every included part laid out.
risks.if_unproven: as an engine without coils and with only the parts visible in photos 0 to 2

risks.risk: Head gasket failure, water in oil or sludge, linked to the rust and grime seen.
risks.proof: Photo of the dipstick and of the inside of the oil filler opening.
risks.if_unproven: as a core with internal damage

proof_requests: Close-up photo of the engine code stamped on the block, readable
Clip of the engine running from cold start, with sound
Photo of the ignition coils, or confirmation they are not included
Photos of all sides and the underside of the engine
Photo of the dipstick oil and under the filler cap
response.reason: The photos show a used four-cylinder engine but no maker or engine code is legible, and the engine code is what sets the price, so the block stamp must be read before even a worst case price can be retrieved. The seller's 'complete' is already contradicted by the missing coils in photo 2.
